Last week, Apple released a carrier settings update to address mobile connectivity issues affecting some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network, and the company is now rolling out another carrier bundle update for devices running iOS 27.2 beta. Here are the details.

Apple releases AT&T carrier bundle update for iOS 27.2 beta

Last Friday, Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network were experiencing an issue that could cause their devices to lose mobile service and be unable to make calls.

Apple said that iOS 27.0.1, along with a new carrier settings update, was supposed to prevent the issue from affecting more devices. However, iPhones that have already lost service will still require hardware replacement.

Tonight, as discovered by Aaron Perris on X, Apple began rolling out another carrier bundle update for iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network, this time specifically targeting devices running iOS 27.2 beta.

Reports of the issue first surfaced in late September, when some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T's network found that their devices suddenly could not make calls, send or receive text messages, or use mobile data, with only "SOS" displayed in the status bar.

Notably, the issue only affects the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which uses a Qualcomm modem in the United States. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple's own C2 modem, has not been affected.

The carrier settings update Apple released last week upgraded AT&T users running iOS 27.0 to version 72.1. However, users running iOS 27.2 beta remained on the older 72.0.2 carrier bundle.

According to reports, tonight's release bumps the carrier bundle version for these devices to 72.0.3, which should extend Apple's carrier settings changes for AT&T to iPhone 18 Pro Max users currently testing the iOS 27.2 beta.
